audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill, Yone, Yone, Skill, Skill, Yone, Yone, which matches neither the packet nor the already-audited Sylas side.
audit.why: mirrorFindings point 2 records the chart as Yone, Skill, Skill, Skill, Sylas, Skill, Skill in both of its layers. The two pages must state the same rows. That reading also fits a 50.34% win rate over 6812 games far better than a chart handing Yone four stages outright, and it fits the kit: level 1 is Yone's before Sylas has a combo, level 6 is Sylas's because Hijack takes Fate Sealed, and the item stages are decided by whether Grievous Wounds beats Kingslayer.
audit.corrected: Set both layers to Yone, Skill, Skill, Skill, Sylas, Skill, Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page carries no cooldowns and describes Hijack at 6 as 'often a wash'.
audit.why: Hijack is 80/55/30s — by rank 3 he can steal an ultimate every 30 seconds while Fate Sealed is on 120/100/80s. Kingslayer starts at 12s and reaches 6s at rank 5, so his heal roughly doubles in frequency across the lane. Abscond is 13/12/11/10/9s.
audit.corrected: Put 80s on Hijack, 13s on Abscond and Kingslayer's 12s-to-6s ramp on the page so the trade windows are countable.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text calls his E 'Abscond/Dismantle'. Dismantle is not in Sylas's kit. The page also describes E as a 'dash + stun', and never mentions Petricite Burst.
audit.why: The real names are Abscond and its recast Abduct. Riot's E text is 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits' — there is no stun in it, so 'his dash + stun' misstates what happens when it lands and changes whether the player thinks they can act afterwards. Petricite Burst is also absent from the entire page: after every spell he stores a charge that his next basic attack expends for bonus magic damage, and he gains attack speed while holding one — which is why his autos between spells hit harder than a mage's should.
audit.corrected: Abscond / Abduct — a dash whose recast chains him to you, 13s at rank 1, no stun. And every spell he casts loads his next auto with Petricite Burst.

audit.why: Executioner's Calling early is right and the missingInteractions needs-antiheal entry names Kingslayer as the reason. The refinement is timing: it needs to be up before the first-item all-in, not merely bought at some point.

edits.after: Kingslayer heals him off you every 12 seconds at rank 1, so keep trades short until you carry Grievous Wounds.

edits.after: Hijack takes Fate Sealed and casts it back at you — 80 seconds at rank 1. Don't spend yours where he can steal it.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Abscond / Abduct's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King helps, but Kingslayer is a 6-second heal by rank 5 — anti-heal is what evens this.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Sylas carry threat 8.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in it comes down to the dodge: Abscond is 13 seconds at rank 1, and Abduct only lands if you stand still for it.

edits.before: His dash + stun (recast pull). Bait it, then commit. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His dash, then a chain that pulls him to you. Bait it, then commit — 13 seconds at rank 1.

edits.before: At L2 you keep punishing him while his E is on cooldown.

edits.after: Early you win trades — bait his E (Abscond, recast Abduct), then punish the empty 13-second cooldown with a stacked Q knockup before Kingslayer scales up.

notes: Fabricated ability name found and killed: spikes[0].text called his E 'Abscond/Dismantle'. Dismantle is not a Sylas ability — the recast is Abduct. Same failure mode as the calibration examples, and the packet did not flag it (suspectNames was empty). Second real error: the full layer calls Abscond / Abduct a 'dash + stun'. Riot's text has no stun on it. Third: Petricite Burst appears nowhere on the page despite being why his basic attacks between spells hurt. Chart follows mirrorFindings over packet.levelChart — they disagree on five of seven rows, hence Medium confidence on point 2 and a question recorded for the user. Note also that whys[4] sits on the Level 6 row but its inherited text discussed level 5; the replacement is written for level 6.
